chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: A believer's emancipation is not [complete/perfect] except through four [qualities].
The first of them is that he be truthful in his narration, sincere in his promise, good in character, and abundant in prayer.
ai.seo_question: What are the four qualities that perfect a believer's faith according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifying truthfulness, fidelity, good character, and frequent prayer as the four pillars of spiritual perfection ('itq), distinguishing the true believer from the hypocrite. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of inner sincerity with outward ethical conduct, serving as a practical metric for evaluating the depth of one's faith. The inclusion of these specific traits highlights the Imam's focus on consistency between word and deed as a hallmark of divine proximity.
